mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a guest suite and an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A guest suite is an attached or detached living area designed for visiting guests, usually including a private bedroom and a full or half bathroom. Unlike a standard standalone accessory dwelling unit (ADU) or full apartment, a guest suite often omits a complete kitchen, featuring only a coffee bar or mini fridge instead. Choosing between a simple guest bedroom suite and an independent ADU depends on whether you plan to host short-term visitors or house long-term occupants who require independent cooking facilities and private exterior access. Bay City Remodeling & Bathrooms reviews these functional goals during your initial consultation to determine the appropriate layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: A guest suite typically includes a bedroom and private bath for guests, whereas a full ADU usually contains complete, independent cooking facilities for long-term living.
